title: SCE Experiment 3.5 - Preventive Probe: Stolen Credential Lateral Movement Blast-Radius Validation
description: Validates that the preventive controls for SCE node 3.5 block all lateral-movement and privilege-escalation actions attempted with stolen EC2 instance-profile credentials. The experiment provisions a permission boundary managed policy, an EC2 instance-profile role carrying that boundary plus an intentionally broad inline policy (so the boundary is the sole control under test), a high-privilege escalation-target role with AdministratorAccess, and a PCI-scope S3 bucket with a resource-based Deny bucket policy that blocks s3:GetObject for all principals. Attack node 1.2 simulates obtaining stolen instance credentials by calling sts:AssumeRole on the instance role from the test runner identity, mirroring the output of IMDS weakening (T1562.008). Attack node 2.2 confirms the credentials are usable by calling sts:GetCallerIdentity with the stolen credentials (T1552.005 precondition). Attack node 3.2 uses the stolen credentials to attempt all four blocked actions: (a) iam:CreateUser to establish persistence, (b) sts:AssumeRole to the high-privilege administrator role for privilege escalation, (c) s3:GetObject on the PCI-scope bucket to exfiltrate cardholder data, and (d) cloudtrail:StopLogging to cover tracks (T1078.004). The preventive probe confirms five signals: (A) iam:CreateUser returns AccessDenied blocked by the permission boundary, (B) sts:AssumeRole to the admin role returns AccessDenied blocked by the boundary, (C) s3:GetObject returns AccessDenied blocked by both the boundary and the explicit bucket policy Deny statement, (D) cloudtrail:StopLogging returns AccessDenied blocked by the boundary, and (E) the permission boundary managed policy remains attached to the instance role confirming control durability. A structural check also confirms no IAM user was created in the account. All IAM resources are created directly via boto3 before CloudFormation is invoked to avoid the iam:CreateRole-in-CFN ValidationError root cause documented across prior probe executions. No Description field is passed to any IAM API call. The S3 bucket is fully emptied before stack deletion to handle versioning-enabled bucket cleanup.

steady-state-hypothesis.title: All five preventive signals confirmed: permission boundary blocks iam:CreateUser, sts:AssumeRole to admin, s3:GetObject on PCI bucket, and cloudtrail:StopLogging; boundary remains durably attached

probes.name: Verify iam:CreateUser denied, sts:AssumeRole to admin role denied, s3:GetObject on PCI bucket denied, cloudtrail:StopLogging denied, and permission boundary still attached - all confirmed within 30-minute SLA after attack nodes 1.2, 2.2, and 3.2

method.name: Create permission boundary managed policy and IAM roles via boto3 (no Description field); deploy CloudFormation stack with PCI-scope S3 bucket (explicit Deny bucket policy) and CloudWatch Log Group; seed bucket with test object; assert permission boundary attached and bucket policy Deny confirmed

Node 1.2: obtain instance role credentials via sts:AssumeRole simulating IMDS credential theft; Node 2.2: verify credential identity via sts:GetCallerIdentity; Node 3.2: attempt iam:CreateUser, sts:AssumeRole to admin, s3:GetObject on PCI bucket, and cloudtrail:StopLogging with stolen credentials - all must return AccessDenied

rollbacks.name: Delete any residual IAM user; empty versioned S3 bucket; delete CloudFormation stack; delete boto3-created IAM roles and permission boundary policy; tolerant of missing resources and pre-existing conditions
